deviation_reason: Airs the long house mattresses every dry morning and takes pride in a bed well kept.
Gathers herbs on the cove shore, where silt in the cove would show first.
Holds that trodh must be eaten alive and argues it with every crew at the table, so she hears all their talk.
Poles the raft through the toll every crossing; the toll comes out of the crew's share.
Vain of her copper horn caps; she polishes them on the stage at dusk to be seen, in earshot of the toll argument.
Won the best bunk at Shells and Stones and likes the village that lets him keep it.
Has the best bunk in the crews' house.
Carries the toll box up from the spit at dusk and has heard both claimants by name; she keeps her own counsel on the state's claim.
Holds the Reed-Sail Compact post at the stage and gives every route from it.
Writes each boat in two columns and knows the levy funds a quarrel as much as the state.
Sells the beds and rope; the agreed price is his living.
Keeps the pot covered against the wasps at the fire stand every day.
Works on rope behind the lodge and meets guests only when they dispute the price.
Fills the lodge jars from the spring each morning and tastes the salt before the others do.
Wins his meals from travellers at seed pods on the lodge step.
This is not her tribe's tree.
Pays for her bed in salt and resents the price.
The Veiled Reed's factors pass through on the road to Helstrom.
Sends the cult couriers and Veiled Reed factors on before dark once their loads are entered.
Keeps the tribe's ledger of the goods that go down the road to Helstrom.
Holds the spring's ladle at the stone lip and will not grant that the spring is souring. She is wrong; the minder and the jar-filler taste the salt.
He weighs the deep end against the season's pay and has not yet decided it costs more than it brings.
He sells every cake to the road crews himself and prices scraps for the smith in the west (record: supplies the Cold Forge).
He has charge of the crew and is paid by the stacked cake; to him the work is a count, not a shame (record: sleeps by the stacked cakes).
From the bellows she hears what moves in the deep end at dusk; she is the one who is right about it.
She stays at the furnace all day and knows the road only as far as the path's top.
She works the bellows from first light and feels the shame of the work most; she says so (record notes).
She lifts the cakes and sees the near mud is worked out; she would dig the deep end and calls the thing a frog (record: pressures).
She lifts alone in the mud while the others stay dry at the furnace and the stack.
She knows better than anyone that each season's cakes are smaller. She tells it.
He works the ford and the channel; road stages are the station's business, so he gives ways by the water.
His plank raft is the only way a cart crosses the ford; he charges by the wheel (record notes).
He keeps the station half's pot apart from the landing's and expects nothing from an Empire that left the well to crack.
She sells dried fish to the station counter and keeps a second ledger of it, as the Imperial families keep theirs.
She never walks past the ford; she gives ways by the water at her door.
She takes her quarrels to the poler and will not deal with the Legion's heirs at the well.
A traveller with her pack held close; the station is a paid stop, never a home.
She keeps what is in her pack to herself and is not selling at the station.
He is bound for Gideon and its courts and wants a paper with his name on it.
He asks every arrival about the road to Gideon and keeps every answer.
She serves an office that sends no pay; she keeps faith with the well, not with Cyrodiil.
He keeps the roster and pay book in Legion form and holds that the Legion will settle the pay the book shows owing (record notes, why.founding).
A pardon without the back pay in the pay book is worth nothing to him; he parleys for the book (record questHooks.opportunity).
She takes the levy at the barricade and would disband for a pardon and a wage (record why.wouldChangeIf).
He stands the day watch on the uphill side, under the hackwings' nests (roster watch-day; creature dens).
He cooks the levy food and watches the meal sacks run down (record vibe.condition: starving).
He walks the road home with every bundle and knows it step by step.
He wraps and carries bodies the Rose would not let go without coin; he sees the families at their worst (record notes).
He waits in the doorway until the coin is paid and trusts the villages' side only after it is (record notes).
She sits with the dead until the carrier takes them. She holds that bones must reach the dirt.
She counts the coins out herself with both hands; she knows the charge buys the bones home and also shames the family (record notes).
He deals with the Rose's families at every handover and keeps the book fair to them (record life lines).
He pays the carriage charge and writes each one in the book; to him it is the price of getting the bones out. Both sides need it (record pressures).
Argues with the stage family's Imperial papers over the keeper's office; she argues against the Empire's paper.
Disputes the tally the stall writes for every lot his family brings in.
Walks the south shore alone at low water; the scrub and the tide are her risk every day.
Buys lots cheap off the other families before they reach the stall.
Backs his family's claim but keeps quiet; loud talk brings eyes to the second shed.
Rope-burned palms from hauling; he keeps quiet about the second shed.
Holds that the rope-stable family hides salvage from the count; a fair count matters more to him than the office.
Prices every mended net once and never haggles.
Stands behind the stall in the yard all day; the shore walkers carry that risk.
Sells to both families and every traveller; the stall needs everyone.
Keeps the stage office; the road and its stages are her inherited duty.
An inherited Imperial office: she will not repeat talk about lots traced to sunk ships.
Calls the vote from a longboat's bow when the council writes; the stoppage is hers to call (record lines).
Casts off the Lilmoth lighter and works the run to the anchorage (record lines).
Sleeps in the bunks below the foredeck with the other three hands (record lines).
Hauls at the anchorage and hears the deep-water crews talk (record lines).
Buys Fish-Eye Rye off the market rafts and drinks it with his nostrils plugged (record lines).
Spends his share on the jaw beetle fights at Archon, not the Compact's dues (record lines).
No guild: mends for whoever brings a net; pays no share (record life block).
Knows which moorings the tariff men do not pass (record lines).
Keeps the tradeship's books; she counted what two weeks of stoppage cost (record pressures).
Sells untaxed goods off the tradeship and lets bunks below (record lines).
Personal: she came to the Teeth from the travelling Nisswo, who teach that each village should hear many readings; one more reading of the temple does not frighten her (faction sheet norm, inferred).
Stands waist-deep in the shallows through each rite; the work is cold.
Sleeps on a bedroll in the upper rooms between day watches; the temple is where he rests more than where he worships.
Keeps the long night watch on the stair above the pilgrim landing, over the shallows.
Spends his days among offerings to Sithis; the Hist seldom enters his talk.
Carries each pilgrim's offering in himself; he meets the givers whom the band only watches.
Meets every pilgrim where the way meets the water; the way in is his daily office.
Scrubs the teeth down to the waterline each day and never past it; below the line is where the temple's dangers live.
She cuts a stick for every load and keeps the count; the camp lives on what the sticks say it took.
She keeps the gate at night and has watched good loads pass on stretches the camp does not work. She wants every stretch worked and is wrong about why it is not.
A quiet stretch means more days at the racks. He likes that.
He smokes the hides and keeps the best for trade; he is the camp's seller.
He sleeps in turns in the hide tent, which fills with rack smoke. He likes the camp least of the band.
She holds the bend by day and knaps flint there; from it she has found walkers Cut-Rope killed on the same tracks. The camp gets the blame. She is right to worry.
Nothing rounds the bend that he has not whistled first, so he shrugs at danger; Guul-Teeba's finds say otherwise.
The bend is his watch. He thinks it the best post in the deeps.
He will not repeat talk about the roll so close to the shed; he thinks it brings bad luck to the clutch.
She says the shed names in order after every shift and knows each family by its hand on the roll.
She keeps her boots on under the west shed's thatch and would take the families to the port.
She sleeps in her boots; she has seen food and broken tools added to the debt and expects to run.
The shed families count him as a hand, never as kin.
He patches mats for families who count him a hand and never kin; the grievance is his alone.
She leaves the first cup of water at the shed door each day; she honours the clutch though it is not hers.
She keeps the debt ledger on her lap and sees the families as accounts to balance.
She serves the house for a wage and carries none of the house's grudge against the north.
She walks the doors for the house and believes the channel work ends each debt in time.
The hatching shed is his whole work; he keeps its fire low and its nest dry.
She mends nets at the shed's corner where every family passes. She hears all the camp's talk.
Buys reed and gets gossip with it; she wants the reed.
Mends nets for fishers who name each bend where a net tore.
His rack is by the landing; he watches every boat leave and few come back.
Sells to the dyer, sharpens at the smith, settles with the elder: he deals with everyone left.
Mends the gaff hooks the fishers carry; trusts iron over worry.
The elder settles what is owed; no faction reaches the forge.
The gang families downriver were hatched under this Hist and still claim it; she sells to their camp and resents every word of the claim.
Holds the trade-house key; the village is her living.
The roll's coin pays for what the trade-house sells.
Has worked the smokehouse by the landing for years without seeing the predators come past it; the danger is on the approach, not at the village.
Will not hear talk of who has not come back.
Her kin-house is kept swept for adults who went down on the roll and have not come back.
She fills the offering bowls and sees each year fewer come to them.
The rumour is her own tree going quiet; she will not trade it as talk.
Keeps a Hist whose bond cannot be bought.
The tree marks every adult on the roll and shows the strain; she reads that strain.
Weighs the tree against what the households must eat; she settles debts, not offerings.
No other income reaches the village; the guest stores she keeps are paid for by the roll.
She has outlasted every diver on the lots and treats the depth as hers.
She works the family lot under the raft and stays down longer than any other diver (record notes); she would dive the deep lot every day.
He grades the catch into baskets by size. Size sets the price in Archon (record notes).
The deep lots kill divers. She is the one who dives them (record pressures).
She brings the day's net up from the deep lot herself (record notes) and knows what the deep lot costs.
He opens the shells for every family at the one table and knows each family's lot.
He sits at the grading table where the tally book is kept. He hears every claim on the heirless lot (record opportunity).
He minds the lines from the tender and waits for every diver to come up (record notes).
He never enters the water, so the lots are only buoys and rope to him.
